# Get started on mps2-an385 in QEMU (Zephyr)

<!-- type: how-to · level: 1 -->

**Needs first:** [Install](../start/install.md)

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED by scripts/gen-board-support.py: starter status -->
> **Status:** Verified in emulator (daily). From the board support registry: [`nros-board-mps2-an385-zephyr`](../reference/boards/mps2-an385-zephyr.md); [Board Support Levels](../reference/board-support-levels.md) explains the words.
<!-- END GENERATED starter status -->

This starter puts a Rust talker on Zephyr 3.7, on an emulated Arm Cortex-M3
board, and shows its messages arriving in ROS 2. The board is Arm's
MPS2-AN385 in QEMU, the board this book teaches nano-ros on: it costs nothing
and behaves like a real microcontroller. Zephyr runs the talker with its own
IP stack on the board's emulated SMSC911x ethernet. nano-ros is a Zephyr
module here: `nros run` writes the Zephyr application for your image and
builds it with Zephyr's `west`.

## What you need

- A Linux host with the [install](../start/install.md) done, so `nros` is on
  your `PATH`.
- ROS 2 Humble with `ros-humble-rmw-zenoh-cpp`. ROS 2 provides the zenoh
  router the board talks to, and the message definitions the build generates
  the talker's code from.
- Zephyr's host tools: `west` and the build tools
  [Zephyr's Getting Started](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/3.7.0/develop/getting_started/index.html)
  lists. `nros setup` installs no system packages, so install them yourself.
  On Debian or Ubuntu:

```bash probe=30 track=installed
sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends git cmake ninja-build gperf \
    device-tree-compiler python3-pip python3-venv xz-utils file wget
pip3 install --user west
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

No board, no cable and no root access: QEMU's user-mode network carries the
board's ethernet to your machine. WiFi is deferred to the Zephyr 4.4 line, so
no starter opens over WiFi yet.

## Provision

Provision the board:

```bash probe=32 track=installed
nros setup mps2-an385-zephyr --rmw zenoh
export ZEPHYR_SDK_INSTALL_DIR="$(nros locate tool zephyr-sdk)"
```

That fetches the Zephyr SDK, whose QEMU boots the board, and the zenoh-pico
sources into a shared store under `~/.nros`. It installs no router: the
router is ROS's `rmw_zenohd`.

Zephyr's sources live in a west workspace of your own. This one pins Zephyr
3.7 and fetches only the modules the board builds with (`import: true` would
fetch every vendor's HAL), plus Zephyr's Rust support:

```bash probe=34 track=installed
mkdir -p zephyr_ws/manifest && cd zephyr_ws
cat > manifest/west.yml <<'WEST_YML'
manifest:
  remotes:
    - name: zephyrproject-rtos
      url-base: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos
  projects:
    - name: zephyr
      remote: zephyrproject-rtos
      revision: v3.7.0
      import:
        name-allowlist: [cmsis, picolibc, mbedtls, tinycrypt, mcuboot, net-tools]
    # Zephyr's Rust support. Pinned to the revision nano-ros builds with on
    # the 3.7 line (it has no release tags).
    - name: zephyr-lang-rust
      remote: zephyrproject-rtos
      revision: 404fcefdbab0f2711cd342a1fab9d2eda52a1ba9
      path: modules/lang/rust
  self:
    path: manifest
WEST_YML
west init -l manifest
west update --narrow -o=--depth=1
pip3 install --user -r zephyr/scripts/requirements-base.txt
export ZEPHYR_BASE="$PWD/zephyr"
```

Last, give the west workspace the patches nano-ros carries for Zephyr 3.7, and
the board's Rust target:

```bash probe=36 track=installed
nros setup board mps2-an385-zephyr --zephyr-workspace "$PWD"
```

## Scaffold the project

```bash probe=40 track=installed
. "$HOME/.cargo/env"
nros new zm_ws --board mps2-an385-zephyr --template talker --lang rust
cd zm_ws
nros setup --sudo
```

That wrote a workspace with two packages: `src/zm_node/`, the talker, a
library with no `main()` that names no board, and `src/zm_node_bringup/`,
which says what the talker runs on. The Zephyr application itself is
generated under `build/` when you build, so you write no `CMakeLists.txt` and
no `prj.conf`.

A Rust application on Zephyr needs three things a C one does not: the Rust
target the board implies (`thumbv7m-none-eabi`), rustup's `clippy` (Zephyr's
Rust support lints every Rust app as it builds), and clang with libclang, for
the bindings it generates from Zephyr's headers. `nros setup` in the
workspace installs the target and `clippy`, and with `--sudo` the two
packages. Without `--sudo` it prints the install command instead.

## Run it in QEMU

The board's own configuration puts the image on QEMU's user-mode network, at
`10.0.2.15`, and points it at the router on `10.0.2.2:7447`, which is your
host. Start the router first, in its own terminal, listening on every
interface so the guest's connection arrives:

<!-- removed when the board descriptor states its default locator -->
```bash probe=50 probe-run=60 probe-keep track=installed
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
ZENOH_CONFIG_OVERRIDE='listen/endpoints=["tcp/0.0.0.0:7447"];scouting/multicast/enabled=false' \
    ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
```

```text probe-expect=50
Started Zenoh router with id
```

Then, in a second terminal, in the workspace, source ROS 2 and build and run
the talker. This first run records the ROS 2 prefix in the workspace, so
later runs of it need no sourced shell:

```bash probe=60 probe-run=1500 track=installed
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
nros run zm_node --expect 'Publishing:'
```

```text probe-expect=60
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
nros run: matched after
```

`nros run` builds the firmware through west (the first build takes several
minutes; later ones take seconds) and boots it in the QEMU that the Zephyr
SDK ships. What it prints is the board's console: Zephyr's boot banner, then
the talker. With `--expect` it stops the board and exits 0 at the first
console line containing that text, and exits 1 if the board stops first.

Without `--expect` it keeps running until you press Ctrl-C:

```bash probe=65 probe-run=180 probe-keep track=installed
nros run zm_node
```

```text probe-expect=65
Publishing: 'Hello World: 1'
Publishing: 'Hello World: 2'
```

## See it in ROS 2

Leave the router and `nros run` going. In a third terminal:

```bash probe=70 probe-run=120 track=installed
source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 topic echo /chatter std_msgs/msg/String --qos-reliability best_effort
```

```text probe-expect=70
data: 'Hello World:
```

The talker publishes best-effort, and `ros2 topic echo` defaults to reliable,
which receives nothing from it. That is why the command asks for best-effort.

## If it doesn't work

- **`nros run` refuses the image and names `clang`, `clippy` or the Rust
  target:** run `nros setup --sudo` in the workspace again, or the install
  command it prints.
- **No `Publishing:` line within 30 seconds of boot:** the board did not
  reach the router. QEMU's boot and Zephyr's start take about 15 seconds.
  Check that the router listens on `0.0.0.0:7447`: one on `127.0.0.1` is out
  of the guest's reach.
- **A build that names zephyr-lang-rust:** the west workspace has no
  `modules/lang/rust`. Add the `zephyr-lang-rust` project to `west.yml` and
  run `west update` again.
- **Everything else:** [Troubleshooting - First 10 Minutes](../reference/troubleshooting-index.md).
